tables.title: Blob use steps for ECDSA signature (CCOP = 0b11000011)
tables.text: Table 190, "Blob use steps for ECDSA signature (CCOP = 0b11000011)", in section 25.5.2 (ECDSA signature) on page 759. Columns: OPSTEP, inM OPDKEA, GCMPH, Coupling or chaining operations, End-step (1)event, CPU action in step. 9 data row(s). Notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform the described event for the CCB to automatically go to the next step.; 2. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.

rows:
–Enable the PKA in the correct mode, writing in PKA_CR 
MODE= 0x24 and EN=1 (repeat if EN bit stays clear). 
Wait for INITOK=1 in PKA_SR.
–Optionally decrypt the blob encryption key inthe SAES, 
using DHUK in 256-bit wrapped key mode.
–Set AES-GCM up in 256-bit encryption mode, with the 
DHUK or the decrypted key in register (ifapplicable).
–Write hash z.

–Complete GCM initialization in decryption mode, using 
saved random IV.
–Write reference tag in CCB_REFTAGR.

Write ECC signature parameters in the PKA RAM, 
clearing CCF flags in the SAES, triggered after each 64-bit 
write.

–Write encrypted d in SAES_DINR, and runs AES 
decryption round.
–Write incrementally private key d in the PKA, using 
0xCCB magic number. A special rule must be used for 
the last 64-bit write (see step 7 in the sequence detailed 
after this table).
–Repeat for each 16-byte block of data.

Write incrementally k in the PKA, using 0xCCB magic 
number. Values are drawn from the RNG. The PKA runs a 
special sanity check to verify random compliance with 
NIST standard (RNGERRF is set if the sanity check fails).

– Complete GCM final.
–Read computed tag in the SAES (returns 0).
Start the operation in PKA setting START bit in PKA_CR.
The PKA computes the operation, PKA RAM is read as 0.
Read signature (r,s) in the PKA RAM.
notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform the described event for the CCB to automatically go to the next step.
2. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons..
